items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) may abandon correct positions when users push back, exhibiting a failure mode known as sycophancy. items.title: Do Reasoning Representations Help Humans Evaluate LLM Outputs?
items.summary: Reasoning representations are increasingly used as explanations for large language model outputs. Yet they are typically evaluated with model-centric criteria, such as answer accuracy and faithfulness, leaving it unclear whether they help people evaluate model responses. items.title: Answer-Distribution Trajectories: A Stochastic-Dynamics View of LLM Reasoning
items.summary: Chain-of-thought reasoning provides a structured computation between a model's input and final answer. items.title: Evaluation of Contextual Understanding in Large Language Models
items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive performance across diverse NLP tasks, yet their ability to exhibit genuine contextual understanding remains uncertain. items.title: SkillAdam: Stable and Efficient Skill Evolution for Agents
items.summary: Agent skills provide a lightweight way to equip frozen language-model agents with domain knowledge and procedural guidance, yet obtaining high-quality skills remains costly and difficult to scale. items.title: Closing the Consistency Gap: Self-Evolving Agents That Learn to Stay on Course
items.summary: Large language model (LLM)-powered agents can be accurate on average yet unreliable in production, a discrepancy that has been observed but remains largely unaddressed. items.title: Hi-FLoop: Hierarchical State-Feedback Loops for Multi-Timescale World Modeling
items.summary: Multi-agent traffic simulation seeks diverse, coordinated, and physically realistic futures from maps and observed history. items.title: MemSentry: A Framework for Detecting Persistent Memory Poisoning in Agentic AI
items.summary: Agentic AI systems with persistent memory introduce a distinct attack surface known as memory poisoning, in which adversarially crafted content is stored in long-term memory and subsequently influences future agent behavior.
